date: 11-329 H (632-941); formation of the schools 1st-4th century H.
title: 1pv0fas
The emergence of the sects and schools
hook: How did a single Ummah travel from political divisions to circles of learning and schools of jurisprudence?
scenes.0.text: According to Shia sources, "Shia Ali", the followers of Ali, appeared while the Prophet was still alive. These sources say that this devotion to Ali was formed at the Prophet's own direction and associate it with events such as Ghadir Hum. In Arabic, the word "Shia" means supporters, those who stand by a person. In time, it became a term. After the Prophet, those who claimed that the leadership of the Ummah belonged to Ali and his descendants became known as Shias. So Shi'a is the name of a person, of the people who gathered around Ali from the very beginning.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul

scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z

scenes.1.text: Verily, those who believe and do righteous good deeds, they are the best of creatures. According to one tradition, when this verse was revealed, the Prophet turned to Ali and said, "This is you and your She'an". Shia sources see this as evidence that the word "Shia" was already used for the followers of Ali during the time of the Prophet. The validity of the legend is disputed among scholars. But for the Shiites, this is one of the closest hadiths to their hearts, which the Prophet gave to those who love Ali with his own mouth.

scenes.2.text: After the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr was elected c**aliph** in Sakife. In these difficult times, some of the companions stayed with Ali. Salman-i-Farizi, Abu Zer, **Mikdad** and **Ammar** are the first names mentioned among the followers of Ali. They stood beside Ali, for the Prophet said in the Hadith, "Whose master I am, Ali is his master". They didn't stick to the verdict in Sakife, they stuck to what they heard with their own ears in Ghadir.

scenes.3.text: The Cemal and Syiffin wars deeply divided the political unity of the Ummah. In Siffin, Mu'awiya's army demanded a judge, with pages of the Quran attached to spears. A group of Ali's army accepted arbitration despite his objections. But then the group said, "The judgment belongs only to Allah", and they left him and retreated to the place called Harura. These were the first of the Haris, and they were called the Judges. Ali fought them at Nahrawan in 658. The people of the forest disbelieved in every one who committed a great sin. In response, the Mürcie sect was born, which left the fate of mankind to Allah. During these turbulent years, those who remained loyal to Ali formed the core of the Shia.

Anti-arbitration group
scenes.4.text: The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala shook the Shiites deeply and brought them closer together. In Kufa, **Muhtar es-Sekafi** rose up in the year 66 of the Hijrah, i.e. 685, to avenge the martyrs of Karbala. He ruled Kufa for about eighteen months, during which time he punished many of those who had drawn swords against Husayn at Karbala. He was killed in '67. It is said that Muhtar made an appeal to Muhammad b. al-Hanefiyye, son of Ali, and this appeal is attributed to the birth of the Keysaniya sect.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 16t2eyg
Al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi
scenes.5.text: His grandson, Zeid b. Ali, rebelled against the Umayyad caliph Hisham in Kufa in the year 740, and was martyred. According to Zeyd, the Imamate belonged to the most virtuous of Ali's descendants who drew the sword against oppression. He also considered the caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar legitimate. Those who followed in his path formed a separate branch called the Zeydiye and in the following centuries established states in Taberistan and Yemen. The Shia Imam, on the other hand, believes that the imamate is not determined by insurrection, but by nass, that is, by the explicit declaration of Allah and the previous imam. The two arms separated at this point.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 19100mv
Zayd b. Ali
scenes.6.text: When the power of the Umayyads was weakening and the Abbasids had not yet fully established their power, Muhammad Bakr and his son, Ja'fer-i Sadiq, established a large circle of scholars in Medina. Sheikh Tusi's work Ricâl mentions about 3200 people who narrated from Hz. Sadık. Sheikh Mufid puts that number at about 4,000. The Jafari fiqh that Shiites follow today is largely based on his narrative. The first compilations of hadiths, called the Four Hundred Usul, are also attributed to his disciples. Shia sources say that Malik received a hadith from him and that Abu Hanifa considered him the most learned man of his time. The Sunni narrative sees this relationship as an exchange of hadith and a scholarly respect.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1ytn1vq
Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
scenes.7.text: In the same centuries, Sunni schools of jurisprudence and kalam began to take shape. The founders of the sects were Abu Hanifa in 150, Malik in 179, Shafi'i in 204, Ahmed b. Hanbel died in 241. The term "Ehl-i Sunna" only settled in the third century. In the Kelam area, the Esh'ari and Maturidi schools were born. There are some word similarities between Mutezile and Shi'a, which gives the mind a wide space. Zeydiye is also said to be close to Mutezile. The main points of difference between all these schools are the issues of imamate, caliphate and which sources of hadith to trust. The deepest disagreement is about who will be the leader of the nation after the Prophet.

scenes.8.text: When **Ismail**, the eldest son of Kha'fer-i-Sadiq, died before his father, or was thought to have died, there was a split over the imamate. The defenders of Isma'il's imamate founded Isma'iliye and the imamate was taken over by his son Muhammad b. He continued with Ishmael. The Fatimid state that was established in Egypt in the following centuries grew out of this arm. The majority of the Shi'a were linked to Musa Qasim, and this branch was named the Twelve Imam Shi'a. Musa Qasim was imprisoned in Baghdad under the pressure of Harounur-Rashid and died in 183. According to Shiite sources, the absence of the Twelfth Imam began in 260 CE. The little mystery lasted until 329, then the big mystery began. The unseen is not death, but a concealment by God's permission.

sunni.0.says: The term's becoming established in the 3rd/9th century; the schools of al-Ash'ari (d. 324) and al-Maturidi (d. 333); the Hanbali-Salafi hadith line; Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad b. Hanbal.
sunni.1.says: The Siffin arbitration, the Muhakkima withdrawing to Harura, Nahrawan (658).
sunni.2.says: The emergence of the Murji'a against the Kharijites' takfir (about 680-694), the understanding of faith, relation with Abu Hanifa.
sunni.3.says: The report that Imam Ali and his Shia are "khayr al-bariyya."
shia.0.says: The concept of Shia; Salman, Abu Dharr, Miqdad, Ammar; Saqifa; the Camel, Siffin, Karbala; al-Mukhtar and the Kaysaniyya; Zaydiyya, Isma'iliyya, the Twelver imams.
shia.0.grade: SECONDARY (the first 100,000 characters of the entry were read; the Bayyina report did not appear in this section)
shia.1.says: Zayd b. Ali's uprising of 122/740, his regarding the caliphates of Caliph Abu Bakr and Caliph Umar as legitimate, Qasim al-Rassi (d. 246/860), the states of Tabaristan and Yemen.
shia.2.says: Isma'il's dying before his father and the reasons for the split; Muhammad b. Isma'il; the Fatimid state (909-1171).
shia.3.says: Al-Mukhtar's uprising of 14 Rabi' al-Awwal 66 (685), his death on 14 Ramadan 67 (687); the disputed nature of the Kaysaniyya connection; the differing stances of Shia scholars.
shia.4.says: About 3200 narrators in al-Tusi's Rijal, 4000 according to al-Mufid; the Four Hundred Usul; the Ja'fari school; relation with Malik and Abu Hanifa; Abbasid pressure; death 148/765.

shia.5.says: The divergence of the Shia sects, the nass of the imamate, the Isma'il/Musa question.
disputes.0.title: 7kdzd7
When was the Shia born?
disputes.0.shia: Attachment to Imam Ali reaches back to the Companions' era in both accounts. In Shia sources, the Shi'at Ali existed in the Prophet's time, and the Bayyina 98:7 report is regarded as evidence for this.
disputes.0.sunni: Attachment to Imam Ali reaches back to the Companions' era in both accounts. In the Sunni account, the term became established after Saqifa as a political partisanship; the authenticity of the Bayyina report is disputed.
disputes.1.title: t0pwle
Imamate: nass or election?
disputes.1.shia: The caliphate and the imamate are the question to which both traditions seek an answer. In Shia belief, this office was given by nass to Imam Ali and the twelve imams from his descendants; the Zaydiyya, however, regards the most virtuous child of Imam Ali who rises up as the imam.
disputes.1.sunni: The caliphate and the imamate are the question to which both traditions seek an answer. In the Ahl al-Sunna, the caliph is determined at Saqifa and afterward by shura and bay'a, and this is grounded in the Companions' choice.
disputes.2.title: 1dy3h6r
The relation of the Ja'fari school to the Sunni schools
disputes.2.shia: Malik's and Abu Hanifa's scholarly relationship with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq is mentioned in both sources. In the Shia account, both benefited from his teaching circle; Ja'fari jurisprudence rests on the imams' reports.
disputes.2.sunni: Malik's and Abu Hanifa's scholarly relationship with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq is mentioned in both sources. In the Sunni account, Malik's taking hadith and his respect are accepted; the report of discipleship rests on secondary sources, and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq is considered trustworthy in hadith.
disputes.3.title: 11h73t5
Why did Isma'il not become imam?
disputes.3.shia: Isma'il's dying before his father is the commonly narrated beginning of the split. The Imami Shia accept that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq chose Imam Musa al-Kazim.
disputes.3.sunni: Isma'il's dying before his father is the commonly narrated beginning of the split. Sunni sources relate this as a split within the Shia; TDV gives his death, his being seen alive and the claim of wine-drinking as separate reports.
questions.0: Partisanship of Imam Ali is described both for the Prophet's time and for after Saqifa. To understand the history of a concept, which sources need to be read side by side?
questions.1: The Kharijites answered the major sin with takfir, while the Murji'a answered by leaving the outcome to God. How do two different answers to the same crisis affect the balance of a community?
questions.2: Zeyd b. Ali chose to revolt, the ring of knowledge of Hazrat Ja'fer-i Sadik. Why do you think these two roads in Ehl-i-Bait separated?
questions.3: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's teaching circle is a gate mentioned by both Shia and Sunni scholars. How can a shared scholarly heritage soften later sectarian boundaries?
questions.4: The sects and schools began with political divisions and turned into schools of jurisprudence and theology. On this journey, how did learning help keep the community together?
summary: The Ummah's paths diverged through Saqifa, the Camel, Siffin and Karbala. Around the Ahl al-Bayt, the Zaydiyya, the Isma'iliyya and the Twelver Shia formed. In the other circle, the four schools of jurisprudence and the Ash'ari and Maturidi schools of theology arose.
key: The birth of the schools from Saqifa to Karbala
notes.0: The sects and schools first arose from political divisions (Saqifa, the Camel, Siffin, Karbala).
notes.1: After Karbala, al-Mukhtar's revolt and the Kaysaniyya appeared.
notes.2: The Zaydiyya was born from Zayd b. Ali's revolt.
notes.3: Isma'il's imamate led to a split; the majority attached themselves to Imam Musa al-Kazim and became the Twelver Shia.
notes.4: The Sunni schools of jurisprudence and theology took shape in the same centuries.
sunni.4.says: And he said: O my people! I've never seen a more learned man than Muhammad".
sunni.5.says: After Ja'fer-i-Saddik, the separation around Ismail and Musa Qasim is transmitted to Ismaili and Imami with the arms of the Twelfth Imam.
